# DSH Studio v0.8.0

This capability release focuses on reliable startup, plugin interoperability and local observability. It adds a
native recovery path independent of the renderer and Harness, Extended presentation mode, an optional stable port,
read-only Host Protocol 1, catalog health checks, verified Profile restore, local budgets and trend export while
tightening update approval, persistent writes and cancellation safety.

## Added

- **Renderer-independent recovery.** A 12-second native watchdog waits for the renderer's first commit. If React,
  Harness, Node or the network is unavailable, a static recovery window can still show redacted diagnostics, retry
  startup or exit instead of leaving an inert blank window.
- **Three presentation modes and stable ports.** Extended keeps the full upstream page while adding a compact desktop
  toolbar beside Compatibility and Advanced. Harness ports remain random by default or can be persisted from
  1024–65535, with conflicts reported before Node starts.
- **Read-only Host Protocol 1.** The SDK and runtime integration expose bounded Studio/Harness version and Profile
  facts to Harness plugins while explicitly denying commands, native handles, package mutation and Profile mutation.
- **Health, backup and usage tools.** Catalog sources can verify native protocol, latency and installability; Profile
  restores verify SHA-256 and present a preview; usage adds local monthly budget status and spreadsheet-safe daily CSV.

## Changed and secured

- The Windows, Linux and macOS release matrix cold-installs the complete 511-package runtime graph and boots a real
  Profile, Loader, web port and Host probe instead of accepting npm completion alone.
- Update approval is bound to the exact reviewed release. Settings, exports, Profiles and plugin recovery state use
  same-directory staging, write-through and atomic replacement; cancellation reliably releases operation locks.
- Keyboard, form-name, modal-dialog, reduced-motion and forced-colors checks are release gates. Workbench, Profile
  Manager and the terminal emulator load on demand, and the production entry bundle is capped at 450 KiB.

## Fixed and polished

- Fixed first-renderer failures leaving a blank window with no desktop retry or diagnostic-export path.
- Fixed cancelled Profile or plugin operations retaining locks and making later actions appear permanently busy.
- Fixed a newly discovered update inheriting approval granted to a different reviewed version.
- Fixed interrupted replacement writes potentially truncating an existing valid setting, export or recovery file.
- Explicit user-action failures now open localized, selectable and copyable dialogs while background refresh errors remain quiet.
- Expanded bridge-lifetime, refusal-path, public-contract, bilingual-document, accessibility and bundle-budget coverage.

## Install and update

Existing `~/.dsh` Profiles, plugins, workspaces, sessions and credentials are preserved. Verify downloads with
`SHA256SUMS.txt`; in-app updates continue to require the Tauri updater signature. Windows, Linux and macOS assets are
built from the same release tag.

No Apple device is currently available. macOS Intel, Apple Silicon and Universal assets are compiled, unit-tested,
headless-booted with the full runtime and updater-signature checked, but Gatekeeper, VoiceOver and installer flows are
not claimed as physical-device validated. Windows Authenticode and Apple Developer ID status depend on final asset inspection.
